evidence.descriptor: Original RV32 stores count at 0x3e902a7c, publishes typed allocation 0x107 at 0x3e902cf4, claims each existing PKT ID under lock28, stores descriptor fields in order +4 zero,+0 packet pointer,+8 zero,+12 zero,+4 status 0x07000100, then stores the 16-bit ID. It then calls the SKB initializer and finally clears 0x3e903974 and writes ready byte 0x3e9046fa=1.
evidence.early_failure: Original callback outer wrapper may return1 even on partial allocation. Existing packet core distinguishes irreversible committed claims from published native queue-head advancement and faults retain both.
evidence.skb: SKB initializes a 4096-byte temporary array for2048 occupied IDs, clears8192 halfword state entries, marks occupied IDs3, fills8192 queue IDs, publishes head2048/tail0. Existing native temp guard avoids reading past2048 temporary IDs although capacity is8192.
evidence.prior: Current RX/API22 owner has exact matching enrolled plan and a retained1/1 metadata effect, but only permits count0 step during API22. Prior descriptor owner currently requires exactly2560 PKT claims.

claims.metadata: DESC10 ownership must cover the early count and ID-pool pointer writes before the first packet claim.
claims.independent_budget: When allowing DESC10 to grow PKT ownership, the expected claim count should derive from a separate bounded one-shot DESC10 progress record, not an arbitrary current PKT self-count.
claims.ready: A native outer return1 or nonzero ready byte alone proves that every DESC10 effect and prior owner is valid.
claims.temp_guard: The current temporary-read guard remains required even if DESC10 has authenticated RX/API22 ownership.
